answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake anchored like a cedar post: each agent must lock funds before it can trade, and a verified fraud finding stains its record like pigment that cannot be washed off, slashing the stake. New identities start at the bottom, a sable-tier trust level that only rises through real completed work, so spinning up thousands of fresh accounts costs money and time without earning trust. An attacker must fund every fake identity and lose the stake on each one caught, making mass Sybil attacks unprofitable.
